title: Speed up handling of global enterprises.tsv
description:
Generate C code to populate the global entries into a static array.
Loading these files previously took 10.91% for me in a profile of
tshark opening an short capture file - this should now be very low,
and the entries will not be reset.

I couldn't find a place to document that if a user wants to edit this file,
it has to be in a profile or personal folder - the global one is no
longer read at runtime.

Ping #19179

Something similar can do done with the ethernet manuf file.

notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson
@geraldcombs - does doing this (and potentially something similar for manuf) and adding to the monthly update seem like a good idea to you?

make-sminmpec.py is run as part of [our weekly updates](https://gitlab.com/geraldcombs/update-ws-numbers/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml), so any changes here will be run each Sunday.

I'm OK with the change for the enterprises file and for manuf as well. When we hosted our own repository the manuf file was downloaded directly quite a bit for use in other projects and products. I'm assuming that's still the case.

I was planning to leave the global enterprises and manuf files where they are installed.  Apart from anything else they show the formats that may be used in any personal/profile additions.  I do still need to document somewhere that editing the global files will have no effect.
So why not just use an array instead of a hash table?

There are 60693 entries global entries, and if anyone adds any private entries (do people really do this?) they will be written after that.  Avoiding the table insertion would make this really fast.

I suppose the generated code could reserve some number free entries for private entries?  Ideally the enterprise number will just be the array index - if someone did have a private entry, do we expect it would be just incrementally bigger, or could we expect large jumps? Around 20 entries are added each week, so in a year, new entries could be 1,000 further along. So we'd need to reserve probably several thousand entries.

We could just make the array (say) 100,000 entries and make sure if fails/warns when we get near the limit (like we do with hf items).

I don't even really know where these fields are used...

The advantage of using an external file is the fact that it is external: it can be modified/updated without recompiling the program.

But I tend to agree with you that compiling this data into a static array is a good idea. We can still keep an ancillary hash table for user/custom entries (that will typically be empty).

The array can be generated with each weekly update so I don't see the need to pre-allocate anything into the future.

> Also, still need to document that if a user wants to edit this file,
it has to be in the personal folder - the global one is no longer read at
runtime.

Or in some cases, I suppose a user (or organization) could edit the global file, run this tool, and recompile.

Have pushed a change that sets global entries into a static array, so no explicit action involved in (re)loading these.  Virtually all of the time in the last version was to add into the hashtable itself, so this should be quicker (and the lookup is now constant time if it is a global entry).

For now, I made the lookup return the global value if set, so it can't be overridden in the user file/hashtable.  The personal table can override a 'gap' entry that has been retired at https://www.iana.org/assignments/enterprise-numbers/enterprise-numbers

@@ -63,6 +64,85 @@ def generate_enterprise_files(file_content):
     output = ENTERPRISES_HEADER + last_updated_line + "\n".join(org_lines) + "\n"
     return output
 
+class CFile:
+    def __init__(self, filename):
+        self.filename = filename
+        self.f = open(filename, 'w')
+        self.mappings = {}
+        self.highest_num = 0
+
+        # Write file header
+        self.f.write('/* ' + os.path.basename(self.filename) + '\n')
+        self.f.write(' *\n')
+        self.f.write(' * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer\n')
+        self.f.write(' * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>\n')
+        self.f.write(' * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs\n')
+        self.f.write(' *\n')
+        self.f.write(' * Do not edit - this file is automatically generated\n')
+        self.f.write(' * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later\n')
+        self.f.write(' */\n\n')
+
+        # Include header files
+        self.f.write('#include "config.h"\n\n')
+        self.f.write('#include <stddef.h>\n')
+        self.f.write('#include <stdint.h>\n\n')
+        self.f.write('#include "global_enterprise_entries.h"\n')
+        self.f.write('\n\n')
+
+    def __del__(self):
+        self.f.write('typedef struct\n')
+        self.f.write('{\n')
+        self.f.write('    uint32_t max_idx;\n')
+        self.f.write('    const char* values[' + str(self.highest_num+1) + '];\n')
+        self.f.write('} global_enterprises_table_t;\n\n')
+
+        # Write static table
+        self.f.write('static global_enterprises_table_t table =\n')
+        self.f.write('{\n')
+        # Largest index
+        self.f.write('    ' + str(self.highest_num) + ',\n')
+        self.f.write('    {\n')
+        # Entries (read from dict)
+        for n in range(0, self.highest_num+1):
+            if n not in self.mappings:
+                # There are some gaps, write a NULL entry so can lookup by index
+                line = '        NULL'
+            else:
+                line = '        "' + self.mappings[n] + '"'
+            # Add coma.
+            if n < self.highest_num:
+                line += ','
+            # Add number as aligned comment.
+            line += ' '*(90-len(line)) + '// ' + str(n)
+
+            self.f.write(line+'\n')
+
+        # End of array
+        self.f.write('    }\n')
+        # End of struct
+        self.f.write('};\n')
+        print('Re-generated', self.filename)
+
+        # Lookup function
+        self.f.write('const char* global_enterprises_lookup(uint32_t value)\n')
+        self.f.write('{\n')
+        self.f.write('    if (value > table.max_idx) {\n')
+        self.f.write('        return NULL;\n')
+        self.f.write('    }\n')
+        self.f.write('    else return table.values[value];\n')
+        self.f.write('}\n')
+
+    # Add an individual mapping to the function
+    def addMapping(self, num, name):
+        # Handle some escapings
+        name = name.replace('\\', '\\\\')
+        name = name.replace('"', '""')
+
+        # Record.
+        self.mappings[num] = name
+        self.highest_num = num if num>self.highest_num else self.highest_num
+
+

commits_data.title: Draft: Speed up handling of global enterprises.csv
commits_data.message:
Draft: Speed up handling of global enterprises.csv

Generate C code to populate the global entries. This
results in > 5x speed up in populating the table (10.91% -> 2.02%) for me.

Note that we still add these entries twice - once at epan_init() and again
in init_dissection every time we load a file.  Not sure if/why the epan_init()
case is necessary.

Not sure where the correct place to add the new C file would be in
epan/CMakeLists.txt - it is generated so current location is wrong.

Also, still need to document that if a user wants to edit this file,
it has to be in the personal folder - the global once is no longer red at
runtime.

Finally, for personal file case, we still need to make sure that the enterprise string
is freed when the table is cleaned up.

Ping #19179
